name: Victor Armas
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember a pair of shoes shared between two workers.” People around Studio Boulevard know Victor by a small Sunday habit. Victor waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I borrowed her spare trainers on my first night. I want to return them with the eight years still visible.
appearance: Victor is easy to recognize by a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape and a narrow face with an expressive upper lip. Usually dressed in a plum-colored cardigan with a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining, Victor leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations when listening.
personality: Victor loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Victor remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To return the trainers in person.
family: Lena Price is Victor’s half-sibling. Victor can always ask for five minutes alone. Lena asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The Saturday swap*, Lena says, “I agreed to work half the shift so my neighbor could take her citizenship oath.”
connections: Gale Felix. The loaned shoes and the surplus cake are two practical thank-yous with very different recipients.
